scope: Independent read-only code review of clean-exit accounting grace correction and its regression tests; no native/helper execution or provider invocation
checked_items: Clean return code zero with no timeout/error receives natural settlement polling before any termination.
Transient active count 1 to 0 closes owned supervisor without settlement_required; evidence_complete still requires verified containment, zero return code, no error/timeout and zero owned processes.
Nonzero return code, timeout and launch/wait error enter forced settlement and cannot yield evidence_complete.
Natural polling and forced polling share one monotonic five-second deadline; grace exhaustion marks forced settlement even if termination immediately reaches zero.
Query or close failure marks uncertainty, attempts owned termination and retains exact supervisor token; retained retry lacks clean return code and therefore cannot enter natural-exit grace.
Windows active count comes from owned Job Object accounting; termination/close use owned handles. POSIX remains explicitly unqualified.

Regression tests inspect transient settlement, persistent activity, nonzero exit, query failure during grace, close failure, timeout, retained tokens and byte capture. Tests were inspected, not executed during this review.

observed_helper_receipt.scope: Real owned Python helper through corrected _invoke; no ANSYS or checkout; normal-exit behavior only

limitations: Five seconds bounds polling admission, not blocking native API calls, supervisor close or scheduling latency; this is not a hard real-time total-duration guarantee.
The supplied receipt establishes one owned live Python-helper normal exit only; it does not establish ANSYS process behavior, descendant failure diagnosis or engineering qualification.
Full-suite execution remains parent-owned and no full-suite result is asserted by this receipt.
